headline: Reviewed plans for Hall Road and Stokes Road bridges, a $2 million Pettengill Road grant, and a new DPW facility.
summary: Public Works staff presented plans for roads, bridges, and a new DPW facility. A 224-plot cemetery expansion will be bid this winter, and 13 water main projects would reach 464 homes. Review of the August 18, 2026 minutes was tabled.
decisions: Tabled review of the minutes from August 18, 2026.

decision_evidence.quote: Review of the minutes from August 18, 2026 was tabled.

A. Project Overview and Presentations - DPW 25

1. DPW CIP Presentation 27 
Mr. Danis the reconstruction plan for the lower section of Bancroft Road, which is 28

2. Facility, Cemetery, and Fuel System 31 
Mr. Wholley reviewed the plan for decommissioning and removing the Central Fire 32

 34 
Mr. Wholley reviewed the plan to replace the DPW facility, including removal of 35 
substandard buildings, improv ing working conditions, installing environmental 36 
controls, and housing/maintenance of equipment.  37 
 38 
Mr. Wholley noted the need to expand the cemetery  and explained that a bid will 39 
be put out this winter to provide another 224 plots. Future buildouts are planned to 40 
complete the project.  41 
 42 
3. Roads, Bridges, Corridors, and Intersections 43 
Mr. Danis reviewed the Hall Road bridge reconstruction project; this is a red-listed 44 
bridge. It will be funded 80% by the Municipal State Aid Bridge Program and 20% 45 
by the State Aid Block Grant Program.  46

 47 
Mr. Danis reviewed the Stokes Road bridge project, which will most likely involve 48 
removal of the bridge. This will be paired with the NHDOT Route 28/Route 128 49 
intersection reconstruction in 2029. They will be looking for ARM funding for the 50 
wetlands restoration and bridge removal aspects. There should also be State Aid 51 
Block Grant Program funds remaining from the Hall Road bridge project.  52 
 53 
Mr. Danis reported the Traffic Management Working Group developed a list of 46 54 
substandard intersections, which has been narrowed to 17 critical locations. A Safe 55 
Streets 4 All grant was applied for, which would pay for a global study of these 17 56 
locations as well as critical corridors. Other corridor studies will be developer 57 
funded.  58 
 59 
Mr. Danis explained the Town received a $2 million Congressionally Directed 60 
Spending capped grant for the Pettengill Road corridor to identify projects and a 61 
path forward. The Town must match 20% of the grant funds for a total project cost 62 
of $2.5 million. The grant is time capped. 63 
 64 
Mr. Danis reviewed three Pettengill Road sewer improvement /expansion projects: 65 
Century Village, which will bring 344 units with substandard septic systems online 66 
to the sewer system ; Commerce Park, a community development project  that 67 
includes sewer extension; and South Londonderry Interceptor Phase II, which will 68 
address failing septic systems and install a pump station. 69 
 70 
4. Fleet 71 
Mr. Wholley reviewed the truck replacement program  and functions the new 72 
equipment would serve , highlighting the m ini-excavator skid steer intended to 73 
primarily maintain Town stormwater drainage systems. 74 
 75 
5. Water and Sewer 76 
Mr. Danis reviewed the water main expansion program , describing 13 sequenced 77 
projects extending 8" and 12" mains to 464 homes in areas with significant PFAS 78 
contamination issues. They plan to package projects to lower the costs  and intend 79 
to leverage as many funding opportunities as possible. 80
